Title: Car salesman jailed 34 days, fined RM17,500 for cheating customers
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A car salesman was sentenced to 34 days in jail and fined RM17,500 by the magistrate's court here after pleading guilty to cheating three customers of their car purchase deposits totalling RM102,050.
Khoo Chiang Chee, 38, was unable to pay the fine.
Magistrate A. Shaarmini ordered him to serve between three and six months in jail in default of payment.
The charges stated that Khoo had deceived the three customers into handing over deposits for vehicle purchases through the company he worked for, causing them total losses of RM102,050.
The offences were committed at Jalan Rosmerah 1/4, Taman Johor Jaya, between Sept 29 last year and August this year.
Khoo was charged under Section 417 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to five years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Eizlan Azhar prosecuted, while Khoo was unrepresented.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK's hard-right Reform hit by fresh scandal as racist views caught on camera
Article:
LONDON: Britain's hard-right anti-immigration Reform UK party was hit by a fresh scandal on Thursday after party councillors and candidates were filmed in an undercover investigation using racist language.
In one excerpt from the 90-minute programme "Undercover: A Year in Reform" by ITV News, black children were referred to as "animals."
In another, a Reform member said his area had become "infested" with Asian families, calling them "absolute parasites."
The broadcast followed Reform UK candidates and councillors during local elections in May and at four by-election campaigns in 2025 and 2026.
Reacting to the release of the excerpts, a Reform spokesperson said that "where members, activists and councillors have clearly behaved inappropriately, investigations have commenced.
"In some cases, there have been suspensions and due process must be followed."
It said the party had "improved and prioritised its vetting procedures, but from time to time, a handful of individuals who do not share our values will initially make it through vetting."
"There is no room for racism in Reform UK."
Labour Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson called the comments examples of "extreme racism."
"Farage can't shrug these latest revelations off as being a few bad apples," she said of Reform leader Nigel Farage.
Last month Farage's long-term aide, Dan Jukes, and Reform head of policy James Orr stepped down after the party was reported to police over allegations it flouted donation rules following an undercover investigation by Channel 4 News.
Farage has faced months of intense scrutiny over his party's financial arrangements, as well as a separate £5.0-million (US$6.7-million) personal gift to him from Thai-based British businessman, Christopher Harborne.
Last year, Reform soared ahead in opinion polls but YouGov's latest survey this week put the party third behind the ruling Labour Party in first place and the Conservatives in second.
The ITV investigation is due to be broadcast on Sunday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Netanyahu's main rival vows to defeat Hamas within 18 months if elected PM
Article:
ISRAEL-GAZA BORDER: Israeli opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Miniter Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival in upcoming elections, vowed Thursday to defeat Hamas in Gaza if he becomes prime minister following the Oct 27 vote.
"Today I give a public commitment: from the moment I enter the Prime Minister's Office, within 18 months Hamas will no longer rule the Gaza Strip," the leader of the centre-right Yashar party said at a press conference near the war-ravaged Palestinian territory.
He said he would achieve this either by implementing US President Donald Trump's ceasefire plan for Gaza, which provides for the gradual disarmament of Hamas and a transfer of power, or through "creative operations" by Israel's military aimed at destroying the Palestinian movement's military wing.
Meanwhile, Israel's army chief said on Wednesday that the military was reinforcing troop levels "across all fronts", citing an increased risk of escalation as the country heads into elections this later month.
On a visit to the occupied West Bank, Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir said the potential for incidents on Israel's borders had grown because of the election period, with Netanyahu facing a tight race to stay in power in the Oct 27 poll.
"In light of the increased number of alerts across all fronts and the sensitivity of this period, the potential for escalation has grown," he said, according to an Israeli military statement.
"We have reinforced our forces across all areas."
He added that the military had raised its level of readiness as it prepares "for scenarios in which attempts may be made to catch us by surprise".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motorists, motorcyclists caught in unusual Bandar Sunway traffic congestion
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Motorists were caught in traffic jams lasting up to an hour along several major roads around Bandar Sunway here today, with even motorcyclists struggling to get through the congestion.
Several motorists took to social media to express their frustration over the unusually heavy traffic.
Among them was Threads user @alvinlai99, who uploaded a video showing him taking an alternative route on his motorcycle.
This followed a road obstruction caused by a car that broke down near PJS 7.
Another user, @yusof300389, said it was the first time he had been caught in a traffic jam in the area in his 20 years of riding a motorcycle there.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Highway Authority, in a Facebook post, reported slow-moving traffic on several highways around Bandar Sunway.
These included the New Pantai Expressway (NPE), from Persiaran Tujuan towards Bandar Sunway. On the Damansara-Puchong Expressway (LDP), traffic was congested northbound from IOI Puchong to the Sunway interchange and from the PJS Toll Plaza to the Cable Bridge. Southbound traffic was slow from Jalan Majlis to the PJS Toll Plaza.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wee refuses to retract statement on RM2.1bil ministry spending discrepancy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong has refused to retract his statement on the RM2.1 billion discrepancy involving the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW), insisting that he was speaking the truth.
Wee, the Ayer Hitam MP, was responding to Kampar MP Chong Zhemin's demand that he retract the statement within 24 hours or face a referral to the Parliamentary Rights and Privileges Committee.
"If the Kampar MP asks me to retract my statement, my answer is: impossible. Because I am speaking the truth," he told reporters outside the Dewan Rakyat today.
During yesterday's parliamentary Budget debate,
Wee sought a clearer explanation
for the RM2.1 billion difference between KKDW's approved allocations and actual expenditure from 2023 to 2025, stressing that the discrepancy should not automatically be construed as embezzlement.
Chong subsequently gave Wee 24 hours to retract his statement, warning that he would refer the Ayer Hitam MP to the Parliamentary Rights and Privileges Committee if he failed to comply.
On Oct 6,
Chong lodged a report
with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) over the discrepancy involving the ministry's spending.
He also called for an investigation into Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's role as the minister responsible, particularly in relation to expenditure under the rural roads programme.
Wee said Chong's demand for a retraction and apology was unwarranted as he had been explaining the budgetary process rather than alleging that funds had gone missing.
He said ministries could adjust allocations within their approved limits, while requests to increase development expenditure ceilings required approval from the relevant authorities.
"Adjustments can be made within the ministry. Usually, the KSU (secretary-general) will discuss with the KSP (Treasury secretary-general)," he said.
Wee said ministries could seek adjustments when project costs increased, provided the requests were supported by justifications and went through the necessary approval process.
He cited the Economic Planning Unit and the Economy Ministry as among the authorities involved in reviewing requests to raise expenditure ceilings.
He added that ministry development committees, chaired by their respective secretaries-general, scrutinised project progress, including whether projects were delayed, on schedule or ahead of schedule.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 10 GOF personnel sacked over drug abuse, misconduct since last year
Article:
KOTA BARU: Twenty-eight General Operations Force (GOF) personnel were found to have been involved in drug-related offences and disciplinary violations between last year and early this month, including personnel serving under Op Taring Wawasan along the Malaysia-Thailand border.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the disciplinary violations included absence from duty and failure to report for duty while under suspension.
He said 10 personnel had been dismissed from service, while investigations and disciplinary proceedings involving the remaining 18 were ongoing.
Of the 10 dismissed personnel, four were from the Eighth Battalion, while the Seventh and Ninth Battalions recorded three dismissals each.
Radzi said six personnel were dismissed last year, while four others were dismissed this year.
"Of the 18 remaining cases, the latest was recorded on Oct 13, when a GOF personnel was arrested under Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 while on duty in Kelantan.
"Investigations found that the personnel had been involved in drug abuse for eight years.
"The personnel is married and has four children," he told reporters today.
Radzi described the situation as worrying and said it required serious attention from all parties.
He said drug abuse and disciplinary violations were serious offences that could jeopardise personnel's careers, affect their families and tarnish the force's image.
He said all officers and personnel should take the matter seriously and uphold discipline while carrying out their duties, particularly in securing the country's borders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Still smiling at 117, Albanian may be world's oldest woman
Article:
KUCOVA: At 117, Qamile Marra is not particularly concerned with proving she may be the world's oldest woman – or even persuading Albanian pension officials that she is not dead.
For a woman born under Ottoman rule, who turned 36 a fortnight before the end of World War II and outlived Albania's communist dictatorship, her focus remains firmly on enjoying life.
"Life is beautiful, like Mount Tomorr in bloom," she told AFP with a smile, referring to one of Albania's loftiest peaks as she sat outside her home in Ferras, about 100 kilometres south of the capital.
Surrounded by fruit trees, Marra has spent almost her entire life in the village, growing her own food and tending livestock.
"You live as long as God has decreed," she said, her deeply wrinkled face framed by a traditional white headscarf.
According to her birthdate as listed on several official documents – Aug 19, 1909 – Marra would be two days older than Britain's Ethel Caterham, recognised by Guinness World Records as the world's oldest living woman.
[[nid:1556180]]
Definitively proving the age of "supercentenarians" can be difficult.
Many of the people famous for living the longest are from places where shoddy recordkeeping and suspected pension fraud are rampant, according to a study that won the 2024 Ig Nobel prize, which awards offbeat scientific research.
But Marra has extensive records that appear to confirm her age.
Her relatives have contacted Guinness and hold a birth certificate issued in 1945, a passport issued in 1978 and a recent identity card, all showing the same date of birth.
Her age even surprised local authorities, who stopped her pension when she turned 100, according to her 80-year-old son Hysen.
"They didn't believe my mother was still alive," he said, recalling how he had to show proof, including witness statements, to resume the meagre payments.
Earlier this month, the government issued her a special state pension to mark her age.
Perhaps the answer lies in Marra's habits and lifestyle.
She rises early to sweep the yard, water her flowers and feed the chickens before settling down with her favourite coffee.
She still enjoys regular walks through her carefully tended orchard with her son, who lives with her, stopping to pick ripe pomegranates along the way.
She also slips basil leaves in her pockets to "enjoy the aroma."
[[nid:1556179]]
Whatever the secret, her son says she has never even visited a doctor.
"She is in good health and has never taken any medication."
Marra's husband died 36 years ago, but she still smiles when talking about their decades together – an arranged marriage, but a loving one.
"Otherwise, how could I have had seven children with him?" she said.
She has now seen five generations of her family grow up around her.
Tears welled up as she remembered the family and friends she had lost. But her face brightened when a niece called to chat.
"I've watched them get engaged, marry and build their own homes and lives," she said.
"When I see people coming and going in the house, I am so happy."
From her own youth, she has kept a single photograph: a near-century-old picture of a young woman wearing a white scarf just like the one she had on.
"I was 18!" she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak gets RM545mil for Jendela 2 rollout, covers 350 sites - Fahmi
Article:
KUCHING: The first stage of Phase 2 of the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela 2) rollout in Sarawak will cover 350 locations, with an allocation of RM545 million, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the programme would involve six clusters, with letters of acceptance (LOAs) already issued to the companies responsible for implementing the projects.
"Jendela 2 will begin once the companies involved sign the LOAs.
"Within the next few months, they are expected to start transporting equipment to the telecommunications tower construction sites. Implementation will therefore begin almost immediately."
Fahmi said this to reporters after witnessing the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Sarawak Government today.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said Sarawak would have at least three submarine cable landing points under the Madani Submarine Cable (Salam) project.
He said Bintulu had been identified as a key landing location to support the development of Bintulu Port and surrounding areas.
"Overall, the Salam project will involve 10 cable landing points nationwide," he said.
In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, the Communications Ministry said the Salam project, aimed at strengthening communications connectivity between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak, was expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027 and be completed by the fourth quarter of 2029.
MCMC is currently evaluating submissions following the issuance of invitation documents for the project.
According to the ministry, Salam will involve the development of a new high-capacity domestic submarine cable system with resilient infrastructure, diverse network routes and backup capabilities to strengthen the country's communications network.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Schools in Selangor, Pahang, Negri Sembilan, Putrajaya to operate as usual tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All educational institutions under the Education Ministry in Negri Sembilan, Pahang, Selangor, and Putrajaya will operate as usual tomorrow.
In separate statements today, the respective state education departments and the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department encouraged pupils, teachers, support staff and other school personnel to wear face masks.
Parents and guardians concerned about the effects of the haze on their children's health may keep them at home, provided they inform the school of their absence.
In Negri Sembilan, the state education department said all outdoor activities, including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies and open-hall events, must stop if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 100.
It added that any decision to close educational institutions due to the haze would be subject to the ministry's criteria and guidelines, based on API readings and prevailing conditions.
Meanwhile, the education departments in Pahang and Selangor, along with the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department, said all outdoor activities had been suspended due to the haze.
Parents and guardians were also advised to obtain updates through official communication channels.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 34 areas recorded unhealthy API readings as of 9am today, with Johan Setia in Selangor recording the highest reading at 192.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'No missing money': MP calls for clarity on RM2.1bil spending gap
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenggara MP Manndzri Nasib has rejected allegations that RM2.1 billion was siphoned off from the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, saying the issue concerns financial management and governance.
The controversy centres on a reported RM2.1 billion gap between the
original allocations
and actual expenditure for rural road projects under the ministry from 2023 to 2025. The ministry has said approved budget adjustments must be taken into account.
Manndzri called on the Treasury secretary-general and the ministry's secretary-general to issue a
joint statement
clarifying the matter, warning against politicising what he described as a financial governance issue.
"There is no story of RM2.1 billion being siphoned off. What happened concerns financial management and governance," he said
during a debate
in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said government projects could face implementation challenges requiring changes to their original scope or budget, even after
allocations had been approved.
Citing a hypothetical school project costing RM120 million, Manndzri said a notice of change could be required during its two- to three-year implementation period, resulting in adjustments to the approved budget.
Such changes, including higher costs, revised project scopes or increased funding ceilings, would have to go through the relevant approval process, including consultation with the Economy Ministry and the Finance Ministry, he said.
"There is no issue of missing money. Bringing this matter to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is ridiculous," he said.
Manndzri also supported calls for the Finance Ministry to compile and distribute to all MPs a list of projects since 2022, detailing their original costs and any subsequent increases.
His remarks follow the
MACC's recent statement
that it was prepared to investigate allegations of RM2.1 billion in excess spending by the ministry if it received a formal complaint.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: K9 unit steps up patrols at KLIA during peak hours
Article:
SEPANG: Police have stepped up K9 patrols at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), particularly during peak hours, to strengthen security following several recent incidents.
KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M. Ravi said patrols, previously conducted periodically, had been increased to bolster security at the airport.
He said deployments were planned around peak periods while ensuring the detection dogs had sufficient rest.
"The deployment is not continuous 24 hours a day because the dogs also need rest. We have to identify peak hours and deploy them at appropriate times," he said when contacted.
Ravi said patrols also took into account airport users' sensitivities, with handlers and their dogs deployed outside the terminal, including around entrances.
A check at KLIA Terminal 1 found K9 units and their handlers patrolling outside the terminal, particularly at the departure and arrival levels.
The K9 units are part of security measures to monitor entrances and other areas frequented by airport users.
Their presence alongside police personnel also allows for more comprehensive security monitoring as authorities step up patrols at strategic locations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six masseurs seek RM10,000 to put Malay massage on world map in Italy
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Six Malaysian therapists who won international accolades in Paris last year will compete in the 'Two Unions Massage Championship' in Italy next month.
The masseurs hope to showcase their skills in traditional Malay massage on the world stage.
The team comprises three men and three women in their 30s and 40s who won one gold and three bronze medals at an international massage championship in Paris in May last year.
Malaysian Massage Association chairman Rosmawati Ishak said they would compete against 170 participants from 39 countries in the Italian championship.
The competition features categories including traditional Malay and Asian massage, sports massage, facial massage, Western massage, aesthetic beauty massage, health massage and basic massage.
The team is seeking RM10,000 in sponsorship to cover competition fees, flights and accommodation.
The therapists have financed their participation in previous international competitions themselves and are now appealing for support to represent Malaysia in Italy.
Rosmawati, who will serve as a judge at the championship, said the competition would also provide an opportunity to promote traditional Malay massage to an international audience.
She said massage skills could offer a sustainable source of additional income for both men and women, with trainees coming from various backgrounds, including housewives, physiotherapists, nurses and teachers.
She hoped the team's participation would inspire more people to learn the skills and recognise their potential as a source of income.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PRISM turns up the heat in Malaysia with Vincent Tan's Berjaya hotel deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prism, the premium hospitality business arm of OYO, is ramping up its expansion in Malaysia, teaming up with Tan Sri Vincent Tan-controlled Berjaya Group to bring ACES Hotel Kuala Lumpur under its Palette brand.
The deal marks PRISM's latest move to build its presence in the country through partnerships with established property owners, as the hospitality sector positions itself to capture rising demand from international and domestic travellers.
The 81-room hotel, now operating as Palette Near Petaling Street Market, is located at Kota Raya Complex along Jalan Tun Tan Cheng Lock, offering travellers a base near Kuala Lumpur's shopping and cultural attractions.
The partnership combines Berjaya Group's hospitality experience and local market knowledge with Prism's operating capabilities, allowing the hotel to tap a broader distribution network and reach more potential guests.
Prism's latest move comes just three months after it forged strategic partnerships with Ahmad Zaki Resources Bhd (AZRB) and United Malayan Land Bhd (UMLand), signalling an accelerated effort to grow its footprint across Malaysia.
Under its collaboration with AZRB, Prism will take over the management and operations of Sunday Residence Inn Cherating on the east coast, extending its reach beyond the Klang Valley.
Its partnership with UMLand involves managing Sunday Hotel Near Petronas Twin Tower in Kuala Lumpur, a city-centre property formerly known as Suasana Suites.
The series of partnerships underscores Prism's strategy of working with established property and hospitality players to expand its portfolio without relying solely on developing or owning hotels outright.
The expansion also comes as Malaysia prepares to welcome 47 million international visitors in 2026 under Visit Malaysia 2026.
With the country pushing to increase tourist arrivals and improve service standards through initiatives such as the Mesra Malaysia campaign, hotel operators face growing opportunities to capture demand while delivering consistent guest experiences.
Prism Malaysia country head Abhijeet Singh said the country's tourism momentum was creating opportunities for hotel owners and operators to explore new forms of collaboration.
"Our collaboration with Berjaya Group reflects Prism's commitment to working with established hospitality players and bringing our technology, distribution and operating capabilities to properties in the market," he said.
Berjaya Hotels & Resorts group general manager Pravir Mishra said the collaboration would support efforts to evolve the group's hospitality offering in Malaysia.
"By combining Berjaya Group's local hospitality experience with Prism's technology, distribution and brand capabilities, we see an opportunity to further strengthen the hotel's offering and reach more travellers," he said.
The growing use of hospitality platforms by established property owners reflects an industry increasingly focused on digital distribution, brand positioning and operational efficiency to compete for travellers.
For Prism, the latest agreement adds to a growing list of Malaysian partnerships as it seeks to position itself to benefit from the country's tourism recovery and rising demand for accommodation across key destinations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Menarabena Asia targets construction supply chain gaps
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Menara Asia Sdn Bhd has launched Menarabena, a digital business-to-business platform aimed at improving procurement, access to construction materials and supply chain visibility.
The platform integrates procurement, product marketing, delivery coordination and order tracking, connecting contractors, manufacturers and suppliers with broader sourcing options and local and international markets.
Menara Asia executive chairman Datuk Seri Saiful Nizam Mohd Yusoff said the platform was developed to help industry players make better procurement decisions.
"The platform is open to the entire construction industry, from G1 to G7 contractors, manufacturers, suppliers and developers.
"It is designed to create additional business opportunities and strengthen the existing supply chain, not replace local suppliers," he said at the launch here today.
Menarabena was launched in collaboration with the Construction Industry Development Board under a memorandum of agreement.
Menara Asia is 51 per cent owned by Menara Rezeki, with the remaining 49 per cent held by Sarawak-based Mexajati Sdn Bhd. Mexajati, together with Persatuan Kontraktor Melayu Malaysia Sarawak, plans to expand the platform into Sabah and Sarawak.
Saiful said the platform would also address order-tracking challenges faced by contractors.
"We also want Menarabena to resolve traceability issues faced by contractors after they have placed their orders for materials.
"Contractors should know the location of their orders from the time the order was placed until it is delivered. Traceability is not just a digital function but it's a core system in the platform," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI worms, 'major' incident fears spur safety calls at industry summit
Article:
FROM the spectre of refrigerator-infecting AI worms to warnings of "major" security incidents at the horizon, calls to prioritise safety in the development of artificial intelligence dominated an industry summit Wednesday.
Concerns about AI guardrails have soared after models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic were involved in security incidents during testing, piling on pressure to regulate the technology.
Google DeepMind chair Demis Hassabis warned AI capabilities were growing fast, telling the conference in Dublin such instances were "early warning shots" fired by systems that "aren't that powerful yet."
"So the incidents aren't that major," he said. "But they could be, looking into next year and the next couple of years, if we don't do more work as an industry and individually as companies and governments on securing these systems," Hassabis warned.
New AI models should likely first be tested in offline "sandboxes", after other companies' models escaped the closed environments used to assess their capabilities, he added.
Microsoft president Brad Smith called for regulation saying industry and governments must "act with urgency" to create "real and effective safety standards" to contain the risks linked to artificial intelligence.
"There are more safety rules for a carton of milk than for AI. There are more safety rules for your oven than for AI," he told the conference.
"We need to recognise that the power of AI has moved faster than the safety for it. Safety needs to catch up. And we're going to need some new AI safety laws and rules."
AI agents should be equipped with "safety brakes" that users could activate in the event of an incident and AI providers should face mandatory incident-reporting obligations, he said.
[[nid:1556155]]
Highlighting worries about the technology, Smith pointed to a recent Anthropic report suggesting small AI models may be only months away from behaving like computer worms, copying themselves from one internet-connected device to the next.
As tech companies race to build ever more powerful AI directly into phones, laptops, cars and household devices rather than running it in distant data centres, Anthropic said such AI might eventually autonomously hop from device to device.
"I mean, seriously? I don't want AI worms in my refrigerator." Smith told the Dublin conference. "I just don't want any worms of any kind in my refrigerator. And I think most of the public feels that way too."
A self-replicating AI worm would be hard to stamp out, because there would be no central switch to turn off, Anthropic said.
The European Union's tech chief, Henna Virkkunen, told the conference AI firms needed to invest more time into testing their systems to retain control over them.
"The competition is so hard globally that it seems that all the companies, they are not investing enough time and resources really to test their models," Virkkunen told reporters upon arrival.
"They have to be able to control... these systems," she said, noting that the European Union has sent information requests to all major AI companies asking what safety and security measures they have in place.
The European Commission gained new regulatory powers in August under the AI Act, the world's most far-reaching rules to curb potentially dangerous uses of the technology.
But OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar warned a "balance" needed to be struck so that safety rules did not pull the brakes on innovation.
"We want to be open, we want to make sure the right people can review models, but again we need to make sure that doesn't slow us down to the extent that we then end up behind the folks who are on the malicious side of deployments," she said.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign student claims trial to stabbing ex-girlfriend, brother
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A university student from China pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court today to two charges of causing grievous hurt to his former girlfriend and her brother in a stabbing incident last month.
Chen Jun was charged with stabbing Leong Kai Ting, 21, and her 18-year-old brother, Shun Jie, in a manner that could have caused their deaths.
The offences allegedly took place at a house in Taman Sri Bintang, Kepong, at 5am on Sept 29.
The charges were framed under Section 326 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years, a fine or whipping upon conviction.
Chen, who appeared in a wheelchair, entered his pleas after the charges were read out to him in Mandarin before judge Suhaila Haron.
Deputy public prosecutor Nurainizatul Farhana Zainal did not offer bail, citing the non-bailable nature of the offences.
However, she said if the court granted bail, it should be set at RM8,000 with two local sureties, and Chen should surrender his passport.
Lawyer Ling Yee Siew urged the court to set minimal bail, saying her client was suffering from depression and required treatment.
"Based on a Sept 14 medical report, my client is suffering from depression.
"He inflicted injuries on his own leg due to his condition and needs treatment," she said.
Ling added that Chen was a finance student and was not a flight risk.
Suhaila granted bail at RM8,000 with two local sureties and ordered Chen's passport to be impounded.
The court fixed Nov 11 for mention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Customs seizes RM162mil in drugs, including 460kg hidden in cemetery hut
Article:
NILAI: The Customs Department seized 1,194.56kg of drugs worth RM161.667 million in four cases in Selangor and Perlis in September and October.
Customs director-general Datuk Seri Amran Ahmad said the seizures comprised 753.91kg of methamphetamine, 33kg of cannabis and 407.65kg of heroin and cocaine combined.
Two local men, aged 27 and 47, believed to be export cargo management agents, were arrested to assist in investigations.
"On Sept 26, Customs inspected 16 boxes in the cargo section of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) destined for Australia and found 285 plastic packets containing white crystalline powder suspected to be drugs.
"The substance weighed 293.60kg and was valued at RM14.68 million, with the packets found among boxes of vehicle spare parts.
"For the second case, Customs found two sacks containing 33kg of cannabis worth RM99,000 concealed beneath an illegal jetty along Sungai Perlis during a raid on Oct 1," he said at a press conference.
Amran said the operation continued on Oct 10 at a hut in a Siamese cemetery in Jejawi, Perlis, where officers found 17 brown boxes left inside.
An inspection uncovered 228 packets of suspected methamphetamine weighing 460.31kg and worth RM23.0155 million.
"On Oct 12, following intelligence gathered at MASkargo KLIA, Customs inspected a wooden crate and found sacks containing 161kg of heroin and 246.65kg of cocaine, valued at RM123.8725 million in total, inside a compressor machine bound for Dhaka, Bangladesh," he said.
Amran said the cases are being investigated under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hamzah: Extend fair representation to all parliamentary committees
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The opposition wants fair representation under the Parliamentary Service Act extended to all parliamentary select committees, not just the Parliamentary Service Council.
Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said that while the opposition supported the Act, improvements were needed to ensure its implementation was fair and comprehensive.
"The Act has already been passed. When we discussed and debated it previously, we eventually agreed. However, we believe improvements are needed.
"For instance, some select committees take pride in being fair by appointing two members each from the government and the opposition.
"But what about the other committees?" he said at a press conference at the Parliament Media Centre here today.
Hamzah said fairness should apply to all parliamentary committees, not just the Parliamentary Service Council.
Yesterday, four MPs were
appointed
to the council after the Dewan Rakyat approved a motion by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
They are Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Baru).
Anwar said the Selection Committee, which met on Oct 13, had nominated the four under Section 3(2)(f) of the Parliamentary Service Act 2025, which provides for two government and two opposition MPs to sit on the council.
The Act (Act 869) came into force on Oct 1, restoring Parliament's administrative autonomy following the repeal of the Parliamentary Service Act 1963 in 1992.
It allows Parliament to manage its administration, human resources and internal affairs independently, while establishing the Parliamentary Service Council as the highest body responsible for planning and overseeing the institution's management.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UMW Toyota sells 24,000 units in Q3, YTD sales top 60,800
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: UMW Toyota Motor Sdn Bhd recorded sales of more than 24,500 units in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026.
This brings its year-to-date sales to over 60,800 units, UMW Toyota said in a statejent today.
The company said it remained focused on enhancing the Toyota ownership experience through greater convenience, digital engagement and wider access to mobility services amid evolving customer expectations and growing interest in electrified vehicles.
UMW Toyota president Datuk Ravindran K said the third-quarter performance reflected Malaysians' continued trust in Toyota and the strength of its ownership experience.
"As the market evolves, our focus remains clear. We want every customer to feel confident in their choice, supported in their journey, and assured that Toyota delivers value long after they leave the showroom.
"We are strengthening the Toyota experience around reliability, convenience and customer confidence, which matter most to our customers," he said in the statement.
To encourage greater digital engagement, UMW Toyota has resumed its Toyota MY App campaign from Sept 14 to Dec 31.
Under the campaign, customers will receive 500 Loyal-T Points upon registering on the app and another 500 points for each service booking made through the platform when sending their vehicles for servicing.
The campaign applies to both new and existing app users.
Meanwhile, UMW Toyota is expanding access to electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure through its Multi-Pathway approach, in partnership with chargEV and JomCharge.
The initiative will see 42 public EV charging points across 21 Toyota and Lexus locations nationwide rolled out in phases in the first half of 2027.
"Of the total, 38 charging points across 19 locations will be developed under chargEV, while the remaining four points across two locations will be provided through JomCharge," it said.
UMW Toyota added that seven sites had been completed, with the remaining locations to be rolled out in stages towards the full network target.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Philippines politician allegedly funded jet carrying 521kg of drugs in Laos
Article:
MANILA: Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) spokesperson Joseph Frederick Calulut on Thursday said investigators had verified that a politician from Mindanao allegedly financed the chartered private jet that carried 521 kilogrammes of suspected shabu worth PHP3.54 billion seized in Laos.
He declined to disclose the politician's identity and the amount paid, said Philippine News Agency (PNA).
A Filipino identified only as 'Fahad', reportedly a resident of Marawi City, was arrested after the suspected drugs were seized at Luang Prabang International Airport.
Authorities said the shipment was reportedly bound for the Philippines.
PDEA chief Isagani Nerez earlier said investigators are tracing Fahad's connections and identifying possible accomplices in the Philippines as part of the ongoing transnational drug trafficking probe.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Etiqa sees healthcare collaboration as key to containing medical costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 budget encourages greater collaboration among healthcare stakeholders, including insurance and takaful providers, to improve healthcare affordability and contain rising medical costs, said Etiqa Insurance and Takaful.
Its group chief executive officer Kamaludin Ahmad said healthcare providers should build on the government's initiatives by developing more concrete measures to address rising medical costs and inflation, while strengthening the overall healthcare ecosystem.
"There is quite a lot that we can work on, such as promoting medical insurance and takaful, and there are various incentives, including those aimed at small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to encourage employers to provide medical coverage for their employees.
"There is also an allowance for individuals to withdraw some money from their Employees Provident Fund (EPF) to make it easier for them to obtain medical coverage. I think that is a good measure, and the onus is also on insurance companies to promote it," he said to Bernama.
He also said that an emphasis on greater transparency through electronic medical records, which allow healthcare providers to access the same information, was among the key measures aimed at containing overall medical costs.
This can help avoid unnecessary tests or diagnoses when the relevant tests have already been conducted, preventing duplication, he said.
"Additionally, there is also a push for greater transparency in standardising charges and fees. I think that is a very good measure because, without standardisation and transparency, there is room for some parties to increase prices.
"With standardised and transparent charges, patients can also clearly see what they are paying for. Since they have a stake in their own healthcare costs, they can question whether certain charges are justified or whether a particular test or procedure is necessary," he added.
On whether the 2027 budget presents an opportunity for Etiqa to capitalise on the outlined measures, Kamaludin said they could help the company expand its customer base and extend protection to a wider segment of the population.
"For us, the more important consideration is being able to extend our services to more people. If we can do that well, the financial returns will follow. We believe there is satisfaction in being able to provide more services and extend coverage to more people.
"At the same time, we must be mindful of maintaining sufficient margins to ensure that we remain a sustainable, ongoing concern. Therefore, it is important to broaden our customer base and to be able to serve a wider group of people," he added.
During the tabling of the 2027 budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the government would launch the MediAsas plan in January 2027 with affordable premiums.
MediAsas is a voluntary, standalone, yearly renewable medical and health insurance/takaful plan designed by Bank Negara Malaysia and the Ministry of Health to offer affordable private healthcare coverage.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said the government would subsidise the first-year premium by RM200 per employee for eligible SMEs, capped at 50 employees per company, which could benefit up to 200,000 workers.
He added that EPF members below the age of 55 would also be allowed to use their Akaun Sejahtera savings to pay MediAsas premiums.

Title: LBS Bina clinches double honours at Malaysia Developer Awards 2026
Article:
PETALING JAYA: LBS Bina Group Bhd has secured two accolades at the Malaysia Developer Awards (MDA) 2026, strengthening its standing in Malaysia's property development sector through recognition of its market position and sustainability initiatives.
The property developer received the Top of the Chart Award, placing it among the top three developers in the market capitalisation category for companies valued at below RM1 billion.
It also won the Best Qualitative Award, which recognises achievements in environmental, social and governance (ESG) initiatives, placemaking innovation and digitalisation, as reflected in its Integrated Annual Report 2025.
In a statement, LBS Bina said the dual recognition highlights LBS' balanced approach to business growth, combining financial performance with responsible business practices, innovation and long-term value creation.
It also reflects the company's continued efforts to strengthen its market position while responding to the evolving needs of homebuyers and communities.
The awards ceremony was held at the KLGCC Convention Centre in Kuala Lumpur, with Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming as the guest of honour.
Organised jointly by Star Media Group and FIABCI-Malaysia, the MDA recognises excellence in property development, with awards covering market capitalisation, financial performance, corporate governance and sustainable growth.
LBS Group executive chairman Tan Sri Lim Hock San said the awards reflected the group's resilience, disciplined business approach and commitment to sustainable growth.
"We are honoured to receive these two awards, which reflect the company's resilience, disciplined business approach and continued commitment to sustainable growth," he said.
Lim said this recognition reinforces the company's responsibility to create lasting value for its stakeholders while delivering quality developments that meet the evolving expectations of homebuyers and communities.
"As we look ahead, LBS Bina remains focused on strengthening our development portfolio, exploring new opportunities and enhancing the way we plan and deliver our projects," he said.
"We look forward to unveiling an exciting new development in November, marking another important milestone in the Group's growth journey."
Lim said beyond delivering properties, the company aims to create well-planned environments that offer lasting value to homeowners and communities.
"Through responsible development practices, thoughtful placemaking and the effective use of technology, we will continue to pursue sustainable growth while contributing positively to the communities we serve," he said.
The latest accolades add to LBS Bina's track record of industry recognition and reinforce the Group's focus on quality development, sound corporate governance and sustainable business practices as it continues to build long-term value for its stakeholders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian-owned Taiton uncovers overlooked tungsten potential at Australia's Kingsgate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Taiton Resources Ltd, partly owned by Malaysian investors is uncovering fresh mineral potential at its Kingsgate project in New South Wales, Australia, after a review of decades-old exploration data revealed previously overlooked tungsten and antimony mineralisation alongside gold.
The company said its review of historical shallow drilling identified 4.0 metres grading 0.20 per cent tungsten trioxide (WO₃) from 46 metres, including a 1.0-metre interval grading 0.47 per cent WO₃ from 49 metres.
Historical soil sampling also outlined a coherent tungsten anomaly extending more than 100 metres, with peak concentrations of 920 parts per million (ppm).
Despite these encouraging indicators, tungsten had received limited attention during earlier exploration, with only about 5.0 per cent of historical drill holes assayed for the metal as previous work concentrated on high-grade molybdenum-bismuth quartz pipes, the company said in a statement.
Taiton executive director David Low said the findings highlighted the potential to broaden the project's mineralisation profile beyond molybdenum and bismuth.
"Our review continues to demonstrate that Kingsgate is much more than a molybdenum-bismuth project. The limited tungsten assaying completed historically has delivered highly encouraging results, while the presence of antimony and gold provides additional exposure to commodities currently experiencing strong market interest," he said.
"With only a small proportion of historical drilling assessed for tungsten, we believe there is considerable scope to unlock additional value from this strategically important polymetallic system."
Located east of Glen Innes, Kingsgate lies within the New England Batholith, a granite province known for its tin, tungsten and molybdenum mineralisation.
Taiton interprets the project as a granite-related molybdenum-bismuth-tungsten system, with tin, arsenic, antimony and locally occurring gold forming part of the broader mineralisation.
More than 100 quartz pipes have been identified across a corridor measuring about 3.2 kilometres long and 800 metres wide, at least 54 of which were historically mined.
Low said historical records show that about 350 tonnes of molybdenum and 200 tonnes of bismuth were extracted from the high-grade quartz pipes between the 1880s and late 1920s.
The renewed focus on tungsten comes as Australia seeks to strengthen its position in the supply chains of critical minerals.
Tungsten is included on Australia's Critical Minerals List. Geoscience Australia reported that the country held the world's second-largest tungsten resources in 2024, accounting for 12 per cent of the global total, but contributed only about 1 per cent of worldwide production.
Global supply remains heavily concentrated in China, which the United States Geological Survey estimated produced 67,000 tonnes of tungsten in 2025, equivalent to 79 per cent of global mine output.
China's introduction of export controls on selected tungsten products and related technologies in February 2025 has further highlighted concerns over supply-chain concentration for the critical mineral.
Against this backdrop, Low said Kingsgate presented an opportunity to investigate a historically underexplored tungsten system using existing exploration material and historical data.
He said the company's next phase of work will involve resampling available historical drill cores and re-assaying them for a broader range of elements, including tungsten and antimony.
Taiton also plans targeted soil and rock-chip sampling across recorded quartz pipes and areas where historical exploration coverage is limited.
The findings will be integrated with historical geological and drilling data to rank priority targets for reverse circulation and diamond drilling, supported by multielement analysis.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aafiyah receives RM5,000 in Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund aid
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Two-year-old Nur Faridah Aafiyah Muhammad Zamirul, who suffers from end-stage chronic kidney disease (CKD) and internal organ complications since birth, has received RM5,000 in emergency aid from the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund.
The aid, raised through public donations, was presented by Media Prima Berhad (MPB) Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) head Mohamad Farris Effendy Md Salim during a visit to the family's home in Desa Mentari here today.
Mohamad Farris Effendy said the visit reflected MPB and The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Berhad's (NSTP) continued commitment to supporting communities facing health challenges and financial hardship.
"The Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund felt compelled to visit the family of Nor Munira, the child's mother, to fulfil the trust placed in us by our donors.
"We understand the heavy burden the couple faces, particularly the cost of disposable medical supplies and their young daughter's daily needs.
"We hope this assistance will provide some relief to Aafiyah's family in managing her welfare and treatment," he said.
Aafiyah's mother, Nor Munira Abu Hanipah, 33, expressed her gratitude to the public and Media Prima for the contribution.
"Thank you, Media Prima, for your concern and support for our daughter," she said.
She said the family had received considerable assistance following a report on Aafiyah published by Harian Metro, helping to ease their burden.
"I am grateful to everyone who has helped us," she said.
Nor Munira said she had given up her previous job to care for her youngest child full-time, leaving the family dependent on the income of her husband, Muhammad Zamirul Zamri, 33, who works as a technician at a water and air filtration company.
"This has been a difficult test for us, especially after we mutually decided on palliative care to ensure Aafiyah does not endure excessive pain and can enjoy quality time with her family.
"Without my own regular income, it has been challenging to cover the cost of stoma bags, specialised milk and travel to Shah Alam Hospital and Tunku Azizah Hospital (HTA).
"The assistance from the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund means a great deal to us," she said.
On Aug 21, Harian Metro reported that Aafiyah was born without an anal canal and vaginal canal, and had a duplication of reproductive organs, with two vaginas and two uteruses.
Her kidneys function at only about 13 per cent capacity, and she is entirely dependent on a stoma bag for daily bowel waste disposal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Musk calls on Zelenskyy to 'go' as Ukraine leader
Article:
WASHINGTON: Tech billionaire Elon Musk called on Wednesday for Volodymyr Zelenskyy to "go" as Ukraine's president, as Kyiv raised doubts over US support for the war-torn country.
Ukraine accused the United States this week of helping Russia by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes and hobbling Kyiv's military response through changes to Musk's satellite system which it uses for communications.
"And so the slaughter continues," Musk wrote on X. "Time for Zelenskyy to go."
Zelenskyy had called on Musk to restore Starlink, which was designed by the mogul's SpaceX company and which Kyiv says has been slowed down.
Musk said any disruption was the responsibility of the US government.
He drew a distinction between Starshield, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications and which he said was controlled by the US government, and the Starlink civilian satellite system, which Ukraine also deploys but is not allowed to use for offensive operations.
The row comes after Zelenskyy replied in the affirmative when asked if he felt "betrayed" after US President Donald Trump announced a diesel-supply deal with heavily sanctioned Moscow.
A senior official in Kyiv also said that the United States had in recent days threatened to stop providing intelligence about Russian missile launches that Ukraine uses to thwart attacks – which Trump has denied.
Trump, facing key midterm elections next month in which soaring fuel prices are a major issue, has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries for the squeeze on supplies and increase in prices at the pump.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Kuantan motorists caught off guard by roaming cattle
Article:
KUANTAN: A herd of cattle created a disruption at a traffic light junction in Sungai Isap here after wandering through waiting vehicles and crossing against a red light.
Motorists were forced to wait as the animals casually weaved past vehicles at the junction.
A 10-second video of the incident, recorded about 8pm yesterday, was posted by Facebook user Suhaila Zulkifli on the Warga Kuantan page, drawing mixed reactions from social media users.
In the clip, the person recording the video expressed surprise at the sudden appearance of the animals.
"Whose cow got loose near the Sungai Isap traffic light? I was quite shocked when I looked to the side and saw a cow with its whole gang! Not only that, it even ran a red light," the caption read.
The user added lightheartedly that if the government allowed members of the public to claim and sell unattended cattle found on roads, they would load one into their vehicle.
Commenters called on the Kuantan City Council to take enforcement action, noting that the junction sits along a main access route into Kuantan town.
Another user, identified as GrayPassionfruit2818, commented: "Sorry, those are my cattle. Never mind, take them, but leave one for me. Do share their latest location."
Cattle roaming onto roads amid heavy traffic have become a growing safety concern in the area, prompting calls from social media users for livestock owners to better secure their animals.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drunk drivers may face asset seizure, extra jail for unpaid compensation – Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is formulating a mechanism to seize assets and impose additional jail terms on drunk or drug-impaired drivers who fail to pay compensation to road crash victims or the families of those killed.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the measures would ensure compensation orders under amendments to the Road Transport Act provide meaningful recourse, particularly when offenders claim they cannot afford to pay.
"Under existing provisions in other laws, if an offender is unable to pay compensation, a heavier fine or an additional prison sentence may be imposed.
"We are also looking into whether the offender's assets can be seized to ensure that compensation is actually paid to the next of kin," he said in the Dewan Rakyat.
He was answering a supplementary question from Datuk Ahmad Saad @ Yahaya (PN-Pokok Sena) on protecting families of fatal road crash victims when offenders lack the means to pay compensation.
Earlier, responding to Ahmad's question on amending the Road Transport Act to provide a legal basis for compensation to families of victims killed by drunk drivers, Loke said the Transport Ministry planned to table the amendments in parliament early next year.
Loke also said the government would revamp the demerit points system, which he described as ineffective because points are deducted only after offenders settle their traffic summonses, weakening its deterrent effect.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Schools in Penang to operate as usual tomorrow despite haze
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: All educational institutions in Penang will operate as usual tomorrow, although outdoor activities will be suspended due to the haze.
The Penang Education Department said all Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at monitoring stations across the state were below 150 as of 2pm today.
In a statement, the department said it remained concerned about the safety and health of students amid the haze affecting the country.
"Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure.
"Parents and guardians who are concerned about their children's health may opt to keep them at home, provided they inform the school administration," it said.
The department said it would continue to monitor air quality, adding that the safety, health and well-being of students and education personnel remained a priority.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pakistan school roof collapse kills 27 students, one teacher
Article:
ISLAMABAD: At least 27 students, most of them below the age of 13, and one teacher were killed on Thursday when a school roof collapsed while they were being taught in class in Pakistan's Peshawar city, authorities said, and feared the death toll could rise.
Most of the victims were brought dead to the Lady Reading Hospital, along with 20 others who were wounded, hospital spokesperson Mohammad Asim said.
The private Al-Khair Education Center school is located in Dir Colony of the northern city.
Rescue teams were working to shift bodies and the injured to hospitals, government official Bilal Faizi said.
A rescue official said the roof of a higher floor collapsed on the roof of the first floor of the building which in turn collapsed on students in classes.
Television visuals showed ambulances rushing to the scene and rescue workers retrieving bloodied students from the rubble.
"We have so far taken out at least 45 children from the rubble," district emergency officer Iftikhar Khan said.
There are reports of more children being buried in the rubble, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'It's like she's still with us' – Irene Sofiya's grandfather
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Nearly two weeks after 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal was murdered, her family continues to grieve, missing her laughter and voice.
Her 65-year-old grandfather, Khyar Abas, said he still felt her presence in every corner of their home.
He said the loss was particularly painful as he had been closest to Irene Sofiya, whom he raised following her mother's death eight years ago.
"I really cannot forget my granddaughter. I was always with her, so I feel her loss deeply.
"At times, I feel as though Irene Sofiya is still in every corner of the house, as if she is still here.
"When I see her clothes in her room, I feel emotional. I have not touched her clothes because doing so would make me sad," he said when met at his home in Kampung Parit Selamat, Yong Peng, today.
Khyar said the family home had received a steady stream of visitors since her death, including friends, school representatives and others who knew the teenager.
He thanked those who had visited to offer support and words of encouragement, including well-wishers from outside Johor.
Meanwhile, Irene Sofiya's aunt, Siti Nur Faeza Khyar, 45, expressed hope that the case would be resolved as soon as possible and justice served.
She attended court this morning with two other family members to follow proceedings involving a 16-year-old male student charged with murdering her niece.
She said the family was relieved that the accused had been brought to court and would continue to follow the case until its conclusion.
"We are grateful that he (the accused) has been brought to court. We will continue to follow the developments until the case is concluded," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman brushing teeth behind wheel flashes middle finger before kicking auxiliary cop in groin at Glo Damansara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A woman who was allegedly brushing her teeth behind the wheel flashed her middle finger at an auxiliary police officer before getting out of her car and kicking him in the groin during a bizarre confrontation at Glo Damansara yesterday.
The woman then managed to escape after a struggle with the 30-year-old officer, leaving police hunting for her following the incident in Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI).
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, the drama unfolded at about 8.38am when the officer, who was on stationary duty, spotted a Hyundai Inokom parked facing the wrong direction.
The driver was also allegedly honking at other vehicles for no apparent reason.
Brickfields district police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the officer approached the car to reprimand the woman and instruct her to move her vehicle.
But instead of complying, the woman allegedly responded with an obscene gesture — all while brushing her teeth.
“However, the suspect made an obscene gesture by raising her middle finger while brushing her teeth.
“The suspect then got out of the vehicle and attempted to attack the officer before kicking him in the groin,” Hoo said, as quoted by the national daily.
The officer called for backup as he struggled with the woman and attempted to detain her, but she managed to flee before other personnel could intervene.
Police have since launched a search for the suspect.
“Efforts are actively underway to locate the suspect.
“The case is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955,” Hoo said.
Section 323 covers voluntarily causing hurt, while Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act concerns insulting behaviour.

Title: Selangor, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang schools stay open tomorrow amid haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Selangor, and Putrajaya will operate as usual tomorrow.
In separate statements today, the State Education Departments (JPN) in the three states and the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department (JPWPP) encouraged all pupils, teachers, support staff (AKP), and school personnel to wear face masks.
The statements noted that parents and guardians concerned about the health effects of the haze on their children are permitted to keep them at home, provided they notify the school of the absence.
In Negeri Sembilan, the JPN said all outdoor activities — including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies, and open-hall events — must cease if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 100.
The department added that any decision to close educational institutions due to the haze remains subject to ministry criteria and guidelines based on API readings and prevailing conditions.
Meanwhile, in Pahang, Selangor, qnd Putrajaya, the respective state education departments and the JPWPP said all outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze.
Parents and guardians are also advised to obtain updates through official communication channels, such as the JPN, JPWPP, District Education Offices (PPD), and schools.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 34 areas recorded unhealthy API readings as at 9 am today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest at 192. — Bernama

Title: Honeymoon hiccup: Malaysian couple’s car triggers Bangkok bomb scare
Article:
BANGKOK, Oct 15 — A Malaysian couple on their honeymoon in Thailand sparked a security alert in Bangkok on Wednesday after their car was found parked in a prohibited area, prompting authorities to call in an Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) team to inspect the vehicle.
Metropolitan Police Bureau Commissioner Pol Lt Gen Siam Boonsom said the Malaysian-registered red car was found parked on the pavement along Sukhumvit 17 Lane in Bangkok’s Lumpini district, raising concerns amid heightened security for the ongoing IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings 2026.
He said Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) officials spotted the vehicle during a patrol on Wednesday afternoon and alerted the authorities over concerns that it might contain hazardous materials.
“EOD officers were called in to inspect the vehicle. They found seven fuel containers holding a total of 40 litres of petrol, but no illegal items,” he told reporters on Thursday.
Siam, who did not disclose details of the Malaysian couple, said they were questioned, and police established that they had arrived in Thailand on Oct 11 for their honeymoon.
They were travelling to several provinces in their private car and were scheduled to return to Malaysia on Oct 17.
He said the couple explained that they had purchased the extra fuel at a petrol station in Malaysia because they were unfamiliar with the routes and wanted to carry reserve fuel for emergencies.
According to Siam, the couple said they had parked at the location to visit a shopping mall after a local taxi driver advised them that parking was permitted there.
“Preliminary checks found no illegal items in the vehicle, and the amount of fuel did not exceed the legal limit. However, they were fined 2,000 baht (about RM243.25) for parking in a clearly marked no-parking zone,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Selangor launches SA500 financing scheme for SMEs, NINE super app to consolidate services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Selangor today launched a financing initiative for businesses facing cash flow constraints alongside a super app intended to bring government services, payments and mobility options onto a single digital platform.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor Advance 500 (SA500) would help eligible companies and contractors undertaking state-related projects manage their cash flow, while the NINE Super App would make government services and everyday transactions more accessible to the public.
Amirudin said the initiatives reflected the state government's commitment to supporting business growth and ensuring more people could benefit from the digital economy.
“In line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s emphasis on the vital role of SMEs in Malaysia’s economy, the Selangor state government is committed to strengthening support for these businesses, enabling them to grow further and compete with companies across Southeast Asia,” he said on Facebook.
Amirudin said access to financing remained a challenge for many businesses, with SA500 intended to ease cash flow pressures and help eligible companies sustain their operations.
According to Selangor Advance's official website, the financing programme provides Shariah-compliant facilities to small and medium enterprises (SMEs), including contractors and suppliers serving government agencies, government-linked companies and eligible private companies.
The facilities include invoice financing, working capital financing, performance bonds and other financial support for different stages of a business or project.
According to Selangor Advance's published terms, the programme offers financing facilities to eligible businesses to help them manage cash flow, including by obtaining early payment for outstanding invoices, subject to its terms and conditions.
Amirudin said the second initiative, NINE, was intended to simplify access to public services by consolidating them within one application.
“The NINE Super App brings government services, assistance, payments and mobility into one platform, making everyday transactions simpler for the rakyat,” he said.
The app already offers an electronic wallet, digital parking payments and access to other services, including bill payments and transport-related transactions. Further integration of Selangor government services is planned as the platform develops.
The initiative is also intended to reduce the need for residents to use multiple applications to deal with different state agencies and local authorities.
Amirudin said the two initiatives would complement each other by strengthening the business community while improving access to public services.
“Together, SA500 and NINE advance the State Government’s vision of a more inclusive digital society and a stronger business community.
“By improving access to financing and public services, we are creating more opportunities for Selangor’s businesses and people to thrive,” he said.

Title: Seven seats in play, 21 firmly held: Zahid stakes out BN’s position in Melaka
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has said it will retain the 21 seats it won in the previous Melaka state election, leaving Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) component parties to negotiate over the remaining seven constituencies as discussions over electoral cooperation continue ahead of next month’s polls.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition was holding talks with PN’s core parties following the suspension of activities by the Opposition coalition, but made clear that BN had no intention of giving up the seats it currently holds.
“Our principle is that the 21 seats we won are not seats that we intend to share,” he told reporters in Beijing today, according to
The Star
.
“If there is to be any sharing, it may involve seat swaps, but those 21 seats will remain ours.
“Any negotiations will concern the seven remaining seats that are not held by Barisan.
“It will be up to the other parties to decide how they distribute those seats among themselves.”
The deputy prime minister is in China on a five-day working visit aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, technology and vocational education. Earlier today, he held talks with Chinese Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang in Beijing.
Zahid also suggested that the prospect of cooperation with Pakatan Harapan (PH), BN’s partner in the federal unity government, had diminished.
He said statements by PH leaders at both national and state levels indicated that the coalition had lost interest in working with BN for the Melaka election.
“We respect that position,” he said.
Zahid added that Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had been entrusted with making the final decision on BN’s electoral cooperation in the state.
The coalition is expected to announce its decision before nomination day on October 31.
The latest remarks follow comments by Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki on October 13 that BN was in the final stages of seat negotiations, with the coalition determined to defend all 21 constituencies it secured in the previous state election.
BN secured a commanding majority in the November 2021 Melaka election, winning 21 of the 28 state assembly seats, while PH took five and PN two.
The Election Commission has fixed November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka state election, with nominations scheduled for October 31.

Title: Pushing mega-projects, Hamzah Zainudin criticises Budget 2027 as ‘lacking vision’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today criticised Budget 2027 as “lacking vision”, arguing that the federal government’s spending plan lacks a long-term economic plan and relies heavily on short-term handouts.
Hamzah (PN-Larut) cited the government’s failure to meet its target of RM90 billion in development expenditure for two consecutive years, arguing this indicates poor fiscal management that could fuel concerns about potential under-investment in infrastructure projects.
The Larut MP suggested large-scale infrastructure projects to serve as primary “engines of growth”.
“I mean he (Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) has tabled five budgets already but still has not shown any clear ideas for the future. This clearly shows this government lacks vision,” he said at a press conference here.
“Even if you look at development expenditure, it was he that set the RM90 billion target. That is in the 13th Malaysian Plan, yet the devex (he’s announced) for two straight years didn’t meet the target… isn’t this the very waad (vow) you made?”
Anwar tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for next year, of which some RM83 billion is earmarked for development. The rest will go to operating expenses, the bulk being pension payments and emoluments.
Hamzah suggested there should have been more for development spending. He proposed mega infrastructure projects such as a major highway connecting Malaysia’s east and west coasts, or new sea ports to improve logistics efficiency, enhance supply chains, and boost regional trade connectivity.
Still, Hamzah and the Opposition have also been accused of lacking ideas. Government leaders often point out that Perikatan Nasional has failed to produce a single shadow budget since 2022, which they said reflected the coalition’s lack of vision or ideological coherence.
When asked why PN has not produced its own budgets, Hamzah called it a futile exercise.
“As the Opposition we are asked about producing alternative budgets. My question is: can they be implemented? If can’t then what is the point? It becomes a self-indulgent exercise,” he said.
“What we do is we debate to correct policies (under the Budget) that we feel are weak and not beneficial to the people, and we feel the views we express should be considered by the government.”

Title: Veterinary extension officers key to Malaysia’s food security, says deputy minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — Veterinary extension officers play a crucial role in bridging government policies, the expertise of the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and the farming community to boost livestock productivity and strengthen national food security.
Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the effectiveness of veterinary extension services should be measured by improvements at farm level, including lower mortality rates among young livestock, increased milk yields and animal weights, and higher incomes for farmers.
“Policies and targets will only yield results when they reach livestock farmers in the form of the right knowledge and practices.
“Therefore, Scheduled Planned Visits and Gross Margin Analysis must be implemented systematically to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions using concrete data and evidence,” he said when officiating the 2026 Veterinary Extension Convention here today.
Themed “Veterinary Extension: A Driver for Productivity and Food Security”, the convention was also attended by Veterinary Services Department director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Noor Hisham Mohd Haron.
Chan said Malaysia’s import dependency rate for beef and buffalo meat stood at 82.6 per cent in 2025, while the rate for goat and sheep meat was 90.7 per cent.
To address this dependency, he said the ministry was targeting domestic production of about 50,000 metric tonnes of beef and buffalo meat this year, with the self-sufficiency ratio (SSR) projected to increase to 18 per cent.
He said the target was supported by 68 satellite farms across seven states, which had produced more than 45,000 head of livestock.
“This strategic direction is reinforced by the National Food Security Policy 2030 (DKMN 2030), which outlines efforts to strengthen the livestock breeding industry, maximise domestic ruminant and dairy production, and bolster extension services as a catalyst for human capital development,” he said.
Chan also outlined three key priorities for the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security: data-driven advisory services, better coordination of assistance among agencies, and building farmers’ trust through consistent guidance and follow-ups.
At the event, he launched three DVS guidebooks on good animal husbandry practices covering dairy cattle, goats and sheep, and feedlot cattle.
“Congratulations to the DVS on these publications. I hope the guidelines will be fully utilised for training and field guidance rather than merely serving as shelf decoration,” he said.
Chan also presented Perak DVS with the Overall Champion award for Best Extension Services, which came with RM500 in cash and a certificate of appreciation.
This year, 78 nominations were received across eight competition categories covering various aspects of veterinary extension services and projects.
The categories included Best State Veterinary Service, Best District Veterinary Service, Best Livestock-Based Industry Development Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project Poster, Best Veterinary Extension Project Video Presentation, Best Veterinary Extension Mentor/Officer and Best VetEC (Veterinary Extension Centre) Operation. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: RM130M boost for local film, music, and creative content
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The allocation of more than RM130 million under Budget 2027 for the local film, music and creative industries is a timely move to boost the sector’s contribution to economic growth and talent development.
MyCreative Ventures said in a statement today that the government’s support would help industry players nurture their talents, create high-quality content and build more resilient and sustainable creative businesses.
“In an industry increasingly shaped by technology, digital content and global competition, creativity must extend beyond producing works to generating greater economic value,” it said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 on Oct 9, announced an allocation of more than RM130 million to support the local film, music and creative content industries, with the aim of elevating Malaysia’s image, creating job opportunities and bringing Malaysian stories to a global audience.
On the full exemption of entertainment duty on tickets for local film screenings and theatrical performances in the Federal Territories, MyCreative Ventures said the measure would help stimulate demand for local works, widen public access to quality content and boost the earnings of industry players.
“More importantly, the initiative will help build a stronger domestic market, paving the way for Malaysian creative works and talent to expand their reach.
